title.rendered: SCE Offering Up to $4,200 Rebate for Electrical Panel Upgrades and EV Charger Installation

content.rendered:
If you’re a Southern California Edison (SCE) customer in Los Angeles looking to install a Level 2 EV charger at home, there’s good news. SCE’s Charge Ready Home program can help cover the cost of upgrading your electrical panel — with rebates up to $4,200.

At 911 Construction & Electric, we’re proud to be a certified SCE installer for this program. We help homeowners take full advantage of these incentives while ensuring the work is done safely and up to code.

What Is the SCE Charge Ready Home Program?

SCE’s Charge Ready Home program provides rebates to single-family homeowners who need to upgrade their electrical panel to support a Level 2 EV charger. Many older homes in Los Angeles still have 100-amp or 125-amp panels, which aren’t sufficient for modern EV charging.

Eligible customers can receive:

  • Up to $4,200 if you qualify as income-qualified (low-income household)
  • Up to $2,100 if you live in a disadvantaged community

This rebate is designed to make switching to an electric vehicle more affordable by removing one of the biggest barriers: the cost of a panel upgrade.

Why Panel Upgrades Are Often Necessary

Most homes built before 1990 weren’t designed with EV charging in mind. Installing a Level 2 charger typically requires a 200-amp panel. Without the upgrade, you risk:

  • Tripped breakers
  • Overloaded circuits
  • Potential safety hazards

Upgrading your panel not only allows for EV charging, but also increases your home’s capacity for future appliances, air conditioning, or home additions. It can even improve your property value.

911 Construction & Electric Is an SCE Certified Installer

Working with a certified installer is important. Only approved contractors can complete the prequalification and documentation process required by SCE.

As a licensed and insured electrical contractor in Los Angeles (License #1027421), 911 Construction & Electric has been approved to participate in the Charge Ready Home program. When you choose us, we handle:

  • The full application process with SCE
  • All required documentation and photos
  • Coordination with SCE inspectors
  • Professional panel upgrade and EV charger installation

You won’t have to navigate the paperwork alone.

How the SCE Rebate Process Works

Here’s what to expect when working with our team:

  1. Initial Consultation – We assess your current panel and determine if you qualify for the rebate.
  2. Application Submission – We submit the prequalification using your SCE information.
  3. Panel Upgrade & Charger Installation – Our team completes the work safely and efficiently.
  4. Rebate Processing – Once SCE approves the project, the rebate is issued (either to you or applied toward the cost).

Is Your Home Eligible?

You may qualify if:

  • You are an SCE residential customer
  • You live in a single-family home
  • Your current panel is under 200 amps
  • You meet income guidelines or live in a disadvantaged community

Even if you don’t qualify for the full $4,200, many homeowners still save significantly by taking advantage of the program.

Ready to Get Started?

Installing an EV charger is one of the best upgrades you can make for convenience and long-term savings. With SCE’s rebate and a certified installer like 911 Construction & Electric, the process is simpler and more affordable than ever.

Contact us today for a free consultation. We’ll check your eligibility for the Charge Ready Home program and give you a clear quote for your panel upgrade and EV charger installation.

Call or text: 747-255-8595
Service Areas: Los Angeles, Pasadena, Burbank, Glendale, and surrounding areas

Let 911 Construction & Electric help you take advantage of SCE’s $4,200 rebate before the program changes.

title.rendered: Why a Pre-Purchase Electrical Inspection Is Essential When Buying a Home in Los Angeles

content.rendered:
When you’re buying a house in Los Angeles, pre-purchase electrical inspection Los Angeles is neccesary, it’s easy to focus on location, price, square footage, and how the kitchen looks. But one of the smartest moves you can make before closing is getting a professional pre-purchase electrical inspection. Electrical problems are some of the most expensive and dangerous issues a new homeowner can face, and many of them are completely hidden behind walls and ceilings. See what ladbs says or the code, Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety (LADBS) & Electrical Safety Foundation International. 

 

A proper electrical inspection gives you a clear picture of the home’s wiring, panel condition, and overall electrical safety before you commit. It protects both your investment and your family’s safety from day one. A licensed Los Angeles electrician will check the condition and capacity of your main electrical panel, the type and age of wiring, proper grounding throughout the home, and GFCI and AFCI protection in required areas.

They will also inspect outlets, switches, light fixtures, ceiling fans, and look for evidence of previous DIY electrical work or code violations. Many homes across Los Angeles, especially in older neighborhoods like Silver Lake, Echo Park, Highland Park, Pasadena, and South LA, still have outdated or unsafe electrical systems. Common issues include undersized panels, knob-and-tube or aluminum wiring, missing grounding, and overloaded circuits from years of additions. Here some details info you can find.

  • Panel Upgrade for EV Charger Installation in Los Angeles
  • Do Los Angeles Homes Need GFCI Outlet Upgrades?
  • Outdated Home Wiring & Loose Connections

Buying a home with unknown electrical problems often leads to expensive and stressful surprises after you move in. Many buyers end up spending between $5,000 and $15,000 fixing electrical issues that a simple inspection would have caught before closing. A professional electrical inspection in Los Angeles typically costs between $150 and $350 depending on the size and age of the home.

At 911 Construction & Electric, we provide detailed pre-purchase electrical inspection Los Angeles for homebuyers throughout Los Angeles. Our licensed electricians deliver a clear, honest, and comprehensive report so you know exactly what you’re buying before you sign on the dotted line. Contact us today to schedule your inspection.

title.rendered: What Is EVITP Certification and Why It Matters for Your EV Charger Installation in Los Angeles

content.rendered:
EVITP Electrician in Los Angeles: Why Certification Matters

When you need a home EV charger installed in Los Angeles, hiring a regular electrician is not enough. You should choose an EVITP electrician — a professional who holds specialized Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Training Program certification.

EVITP certification ensures your installer understands the unique requirements of EV charging systems. This training helps you avoid safety issues, pass inspections the first time, and qualify for valuable rebates.

What Makes an EVITP Electrician Different?

EVITP is a rigorous national certification program designed specifically for electric vehicle supply equipment (EVSE). Certified electricians receive advanced training on:

  • Proper high-voltage wiring for EV chargers
  • National Electrical Code (NEC) Article 625 requirements
  • Load calculations and panel capacity assessments
  • Smart charger integration and safety protocols
  • Grounding, bonding, and GFCI protection standards

This specialized knowledge goes far beyond a standard electrical license.

Why You Should Hire an EVITP Electrician in Los Angeles

  • Rebate Qualification — LADWP, Pasadena Water & Power, and many California incentives require EVITP certification to approve rebates up to $1,500.
  • Safety First — EV chargers involve high power. Proper installation prevents overheating, fire hazards, and electrical faults.
  • Faster Approvals — Certified installers know local permitting rules, so your project moves quickly through inspections.
  • Future-Proof Results — You get a reliable system that supports today’s and tomorrow’s electric vehicles.
  • Warranty Protection — Many charger manufacturers require certified installers to keep your warranty valid.

Our EVITP Certified Electricians in Los Angeles

At 911 Construction & Electric (California License #1027421), our electricians are fully EVITP certified. We provide expert EV charger installation services across Los Angeles, Burbank, Pasadena, Glendale, Hollywood, and surrounding cities.

We handle the complete process:

  • Free site evaluation and electrical load assessment
  • Panel upgrades when needed
  • Professional Level 2 charger installation (hardwired or plug-in)
  • Smart Wi-Fi enabled chargers with app control
  • Full permitting and inspections
  • Rebate paperwork assistance
  • Same-day and next-day scheduling
  • 24/7 emergency electrical support

Ready for Professional EV Charger Installation?

Don’t risk your safety or rebate eligibility with a non-certified installer. Hire experienced EVITP electricians who specialize in this work.

Contact us today for a free quote on EV charger installation in Los Angeles.

Call Now: 747-255-8595

title.rendered: 7 Warning Signs Your Los Angeles Home Needs Rewiring

content.rendered:
“If you’re concerned about home rewiring in Los Angeles, you’re not alone. Many homes across Los Angeles — especially those built before the 1980s in areas like Burbank, Glendale, and Pasadena — are still running on outdated electrical wiring. While the lights may work just fine, aging wiring can create hidden hazards behind your walls that pose a serious fire and safety risk.

At 911 Construction & Electric Inc. (CSLB #1027421), we’ve inspected hundreds of homes across Los Angeles County and consistently find the same warning signs that homeowners overlook. Here’s what to watch for — and when it’s time to call a professional.

Why Rewiring Matters in Los Angeles

California’s electrical code has been updated significantly over the decades. Homes built before 1980 may have aluminum wiring, knob-and-tube systems, or undersized panels that weren’t designed for today’s electrical demands — think multiple TVs, EV chargers, air conditioning units, and home offices running simultaneously.

According to the U.S. Fire Administration, electrical fires account for an estimated 51,000 home fires each year. Outdated wiring is one of the top contributing factors — and many of these fires are entirely preventable.

1. Flickering or Dimming Lights

If your lights dim or flicker when you turn on a large appliance — like your air conditioner, washer, or microwave — it’s a sign that your electrical circuits are struggling to handle the load. In Los Angeles, where summers push AC units hard, this is a very common complaint we hear from homeowners in Burbank and Pasadena.

While a single flickering bulb might just be a loose fitting, lights dimming throughout the house point to a deeper wiring or panel issue that requires professional inspection.

2. Breakers That Trip Frequently

Circuit breakers are designed to trip as a safety mechanism — but if yours are tripping regularly, that’s not normal operation. It means the circuit is consistently overloaded, which can degrade wiring over time and create a fire hazard.

If a breaker trips once after heavy use, reset it. If it keeps tripping or won’t reset at all, call a licensed electrician. Never replace a breaker with a higher-rated one yourself — this removes the safety protection entirely.

3. Burning Smells or Scorch Marks Near Outlets

This is the most urgent warning sign on this list. A burning smell — even faint — near an outlet, switch, or panel could mean wiring is overheating behind your walls. Scorch marks or discoloration around outlet faceplates confirm heat damage has already occurred.

If you smell burning near any outlet or panel, stop using that circuit and call an electrician right away. This is not a situation to monitor — it is a potential fire hazard that needs immediate attention.

4. Sparks When Plugging In Devices

A very brief, tiny spark when plugging in a device can be normal — it’s just electricity making contact. But large, frequent, or long-lasting sparks are abnormal and indicate a loose connection, short circuit, or moisture issue inside the outlet. Any sparking that concerns you should be inspected by a licensed electrician.

5. Outlets or Switch Plates That Are Warm to the Touch

Outlets and switches should always be at room temperature. If they feel warm — or if you hear buzzing or crackling sounds coming from the wall — wiring inside may be arcing or overheating. This is a code violation and a fire risk that should be addressed immediately.

6. Your Home Was Built Before 1980

Many Los Angeles neighborhoods — including parts of Glendale, Burbank, and the San Fernando Valley — have large stocks of homes built in the 1950s through 1970s. These homes may have:

  • Aluminum wiring — expands and contracts differently than copper and can loosen over time, creating arcing hazards
  • Knob-and-tube wiring — lacks a ground wire and wasn’t designed for modern electrical loads
  • 60-amp panels — drastically undersized for today’s homes; most modern households need 200 amps minimum
  • No GFCI or AFCI protection — now required in kitchens, bathrooms, garages, and outdoor areas under California code

If your home falls into this category, a professional electrical inspection is strongly recommended even if you haven’t noticed any obvious problems.

7. Two-Prong (Ungrounded) Outlets Throughout the Home

If most or all of your outlets have only two slots (no round grounding hole), your wiring predates modern safety standards. Ungrounded outlets can damage sensitive electronics and pose a shock risk. Upgrading to grounded three-prong outlets requires proper grounding — not just swapping the faceplate.

What Does Home Rewiring Cost in Los Angeles?

The cost varies depending on the size of the home, the type of existing wiring, and the scope of work. A typical Los Angeles home rewire ranges from a targeted circuit upgrade to a full panel replacement and whole-home rewire.

Rewiring a home in Los Angeles doesn’t always mean tearing out every wall. Our team at 911 Construction & Electric uses low-impact techniques to run new wiring with minimal disruption — and we handle all permits and inspections required by Los Angeles County.

We always provide a detailed written quote before any work begins — no surprises.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I know if my home has aluminum wiring?
The easiest way is to have a licensed electrician inspect your panel and outlets. You may also see “AL” stamped on the wire jacket in your panel or attic. Aluminum wiring is silver-colored rather than copper-colored.

Do I need a permit to rewire my home in Los Angeles?
Yes. Any significant electrical work in Los Angeles County requires a permit from the Department of Building and Safety (LADBS). At 911 Construction & Electric Inc., we handle all permitting and inspections as part of every project.

How long does a home rewire take?
A full rewire of an average-sized Los Angeles home typically takes 3 to 7 days depending on the size and complexity. We work efficiently to minimize disruption and keep your home livable throughout the process where possible.

Will my homeowner’s insurance cover rewiring?
In most cases, no — insurance covers damage from electrical failures, not the rewiring itself. However, some insurers offer discounts after a certified rewire, and some may require updated wiring to maintain coverage on older homes. Check with your provider.

Can I stay in my home while it’s being rewired?
In many cases, yes. We plan the work in phases to keep most of your home powered during the project. Our team will walk you through what to expect before work begins.

Concerned About Your Home’s Wiring? Contact Us Today

911 Construction & Electric Inc. serves Los Angeles, Burbank, Glendale, Pasadena, Altadena, and all surrounding areas. Our licensed electricians provide free written quotes with no obligation.

title.rendered: How to Choose a Licensed Electrician: The Complete Guide for Homeowners and Businesses

content.rendered:
Hiring the wrong electrician can cost you thousands — or worse, put your property at serious risk. Whether you need residential electrical work or a full commercial installation, choosing a licensed electrician in Los Angeles is the most important decision you’ll make for your project.

At 911 Construction & Electric Inc. (CSLB #1027421), we believe every customer deserves to make an informed choice. Here’s exactly what to look for before you hire.

Always Verify Their Licence

The very first thing you should ask any electrician is for their licence number. A legitimate licensed electrician will provide this without hesitation. In California, electrical licences are issued by the Contractors State License Board (CSLB) and can be verified online at their official website.

Unlicensed electrical work is illegal in California. It voids your home insurance, fails building inspections, and creates serious liability if something goes wrong. Always verify before work begins.

Check for Insurance and Public Liability Cover

Licensing and insurance are two separate things. A licensed electrician should also carry public liability insurance and, if they employ others, workers’ compensation coverage. Without these, you could be held liable for any damage or injuries that occur on your property during the job.

Always ask for a copy of their Certificate of Currency — a one-page document from their insurer confirming active coverage. A reputable electrician will have it on hand.

Residential vs. Commercial: Know the Difference

Not all electricians work across both sectors. Residential electrical work involves household wiring, safety switches, lighting, and appliance circuits. Commercial electrical work involves three-phase power, high-load switchboards, industrial equipment, and compliance with different safety standards.

If you’re a business owner or property developer in Los Angeles, confirm that the electrician has specific commercial experience and can provide examples of similar projects. Don’t assume residential experience translates directly to commercial work.

Get Multiple Written Quotes

Verbal estimates are worth little. Always request a written quote that breaks down labour, materials, and any call-out fees. Getting at least two or three quotes gives you a realistic price range and helps you spot any outliers — whether suspiciously cheap or unexpectedly expensive.

If an electrician refuses to provide a written quote or pressures you to sign on the spot, walk away. Reputable tradespeople don’t operate that way.

Read Reviews and Ask for References

Online reviews on Google offer a genuine window into how a business operates. Look for patterns across multiple reviews rather than focusing on a single rating. Consistently positive mentions of punctuality, cleanliness, and communication are strong signals of a trustworthy contractor.

For larger commercial jobs, don’t hesitate to ask the electrician directly for references you can call. A company that has completed successful projects will be proud to share them.

Confirm They Provide a Certificate of Compliance

After any significant electrical work, a licensed electrician is required to issue a Certificate of Electrical Compliance. This document confirms the work meets the required safety standards and has been tested. You’ll need it for insurance purposes and when selling your property.

If an electrician does not mention a certificate of compliance, ask for it directly before signing off on any job. It is your legal right to receive one in California.

Red Flags to Watch For

Before hiring any electrician in Los Angeles, watch out for these warning signs:

  • No licence number or reluctance to share it
  • Quotes that are dramatically lower than competitors
  • No written contract or quote provided
  • No proof of insurance
  • Pressure to pay entirely in cash with no receipt
  • Unable to provide a certificate of compliance after the job

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need a licensed electrician for small jobs?
Yes. In California, any electrical work beyond changing a light bulb must be done by a licensed electrician. Even small work like adding a power point or replacing a switchboard component requires proper licensing and a certificate of compliance.

How much does a licensed electrician cost in Los Angeles?
Costs vary depending on the job, your location, and the complexity of the work. Most electricians charge an hourly rate plus materials, with a call-out fee for smaller jobs. At 911 Construction & Electric, we always provide a free written quote before any work begins.

What’s the difference between a licensed electrician and an apprentice?
A licensed electrician has completed their full trade qualification and is legally permitted to work independently. Apprentices can assist on-site but must be supervised by a licensed electrician at all times. All work must be signed off by the licensed professional.

Can I do my own electrical work in California?
In almost all cases, no. DIY electrical work is illegal in California and can void your insurance, fail inspections, and create serious safety hazards. Always hire a licensed professional.

Need a Licensed Electrician in Los Angeles?

911 Construction & Electric Inc. serves Los Angeles, Burbank, Glendale, Pasadena, and all surrounding areas. Our licensed electricians handle residential and commercial electrical work — from safety inspections to full fit-outs. We handle all permits and inspections required by Los Angeles County.

License #1027421 | Available 24/7 | (747) 255-8595

Contact us today

title.rendered: Outdated Home Wiring & Loose Connections: Why Southern California Homeowners Should Check Now

content.rendered:
Outdated Home Wiring & Loose Electrical Connections in Los Angeles: Warning Signs Homeowners Shouldn’t Ignore

Older homes across Los Angeles, Pasadena, Glendale, Burbank, and the San Fernando Valley often have hidden electrical issues that homeowners never notice until a serious problem appears. Outdated wiring and loose electrical connections can increase the risk of electrical fires, damaged appliances, flickering lights, overloaded circuits, and power failures.

Many Southern California homes were built decades ago. Electrical systems in older properties may no longer meet today’s power demands. Modern homes use more appliances, electronics, EV chargers, air conditioning systems, and smart devices than older electrical systems were designed to handle.

If your home shows signs of electrical problems, scheduling a professional electrical inspection can help identify safety hazards before they become expensive repairs.

Signs Your Home May Have Outdated Wiring

Older electrical systems often show warning signs before major failures happen. Homeowners should pay attention to these common issues:

  • Flickering or dimming lights
  • Frequently tripped breakers
  • Warm outlets or switches
  • Buzzing sounds from outlets or panels
  • Burning smells near electrical components
  • Two-prong outlets
  • Discolored outlets or switch plates
  • Power fluctuations when appliances turn on
  • Extension cords used throughout the home

These symptoms may indicate loose electrical connections, overloaded circuits, deteriorating wiring, or outdated electrical panels.

Why Loose Electrical Connections Are Dangerous

Loose electrical connections create heat. Over time, heat damages wires, outlets, switches, and breakers. In severe cases, loose wiring can start electrical fires inside walls where homeowners cannot see the danger.

Connections may loosen because of:

  • Aging electrical components
  • Improper installations
  • Vibration from daily electrical use
  • Corrosion
  • Poor maintenance
  • Overloaded circuits

Even small connection problems can become major safety hazards if they are ignored.

Common Electrical Problems in Older Southern California Homes

Homes built several decades ago often contain outdated electrical materials or systems that no longer meet current safety standards.

Common issues include:

Aluminum Wiring

Some older homes contain aluminum wiring, which expands and contracts more than copper wiring. This movement can loosen electrical connections and increase fire risks.

Outdated Electrical Panels

Older electrical panels may struggle to handle modern energy usage. Homes with upgraded appliances or EV chargers often need panel upgrades to safely support higher electrical loads.

Ungrounded Outlets

Many older homes still have two-prong outlets without proper grounding protection. Ungrounded outlets increase the risk of shocks and equipment damage.

Worn or Damaged Wiring

Electrical wiring naturally deteriorates over time. Heat, rodents, moisture, and aging insulation can all damage wiring behind walls.

Electrical Fires Often Start Behind Walls

One of the biggest dangers of outdated wiring is that problems remain hidden until significant damage occurs. Loose connections and damaged wiring frequently develop inside walls, attics, crawl spaces, or electrical panels.

Homeowners may not notice issues until they experience:

  • Partial power loss
  • Burning odors
  • Smoke
  • Sparking outlets
  • Dead outlets
  • Circuit breaker failures

Professional electrical inspections help identify hidden problems early.

Why Older Homes Need Electrical Inspections

A licensed electrician can inspect your electrical system and identify safety concerns before they become emergencies.

An electrical safety inspection may include:

  • Checking electrical panels
  • Inspecting wiring conditions
  • Testing outlets and breakers
  • Identifying overloaded circuits
  • Examining grounding systems
  • Finding loose electrical connections
  • Evaluating fire hazards

Inspections are especially important before purchasing an older home, remodeling, installing new appliances, or adding an EV charger.

When to Consider Rewiring Your Home

Complete rewiring is not always necessary, but some homes benefit from partial or full electrical upgrades.

You may need rewiring if your home has:

  • Frequent breaker trips
  • Old cloth wiring
  • Aluminum wiring
  • Unsafe electrical panels
  • Extensive extension cord use
  • Burning smells or sparks
  • Aging electrical infrastructure

Upgrading your electrical system improves safety, reliability, and home value.

Protect Your Home With Professional Electrical Service

Electrical issues should never be ignored. Small wiring problems can quickly become serious safety hazards.

Whether you need an electrical inspection, wiring repair, panel upgrade, or troubleshooting service, working with a licensed electrician helps protect your home and family.

911 Electrics provides electrical inspections, wiring repairs, panel upgrades, EV charger installations, and electrical safety services throughout Los Angeles, Pasadena, Glendale, Burbank, and surrounding Southern California communities.

FAQ About Outdated Home Wiring

How do I know if my home has outdated wiring?

Common warning signs include flickering lights, warm outlets, frequent breaker trips, buzzing sounds, and older two-prong outlets.

title.rendered: Why a Panel Upgrade Can Save Money in Pasadena and Nearby Los Angeles Areas

content.rendered:
If you’re planning to install an EV charger in Pasadena or nearby Los Angeles areas, you may have heard that a panel upgrade is often required. Many older homes still have 100-amp electrical panels that can’t safely handle the added load of a Level 2 charger. Upgrading your panel not only makes the installation possible, but it can also save you money in the long run through rebates, incentives, and avoided repairs. A proper panel upgrade is one of the smartest investments you can make when adding EV charging to your home.

Why Most Homes Need a Panel Upgrade for EV Chargers

Most homes built before 2000 have 100-amp panels. These panels were never designed to support modern electrical demands like central air conditioning, electric water heaters, and now EV chargers. Adding a Level 2 charger without upgrading can lead to frequent breaker trips, overheating, and serious safety risks. A panel upgrade to 200 amps provides the capacity and safety needed for EV charging and future electrical needs. Without this upgrade, your electrical system may struggle to keep up with the increased demand and could create dangerous situations over time.

How Panel Upgrades Help You Qualify for Rebates

Many rebate and incentive programs in Pasadena and Los Angeles require a properly upgraded electrical panel. Without the upgrade, you may not qualify for thousands of dollars in available rebates. A panel upgrade can also make your home eligible for additional energy efficiency programs that further reduce your overall costs. These programs are designed to encourage EV adoption and reward homeowners who make their homes more energy efficient and environmentally friendly.

Long-Term Savings and Home Value

Beyond rebates, a panel upgrade helps you avoid expensive emergency repairs and electrical issues down the road. It also increases your home’s value and appeal to future buyers who want an EV-ready property. Homes with upgraded electrical systems and EV charging capability often sell faster and for higher prices in the current market. Buyers are increasingly looking for homes that are already prepared for electric vehicles and modern electrical needs.

Additional Benefits of Upgrading Your Panel

  • Improved safety and reduced risk of electrical fires
  • Better support for future appliances and technology
  • Higher energy efficiency and lower utility bills
  • Easier qualification for solar and battery storage systems
  • Increased peace of mind knowing your electrical system is up to code

Let 911 Construction & Electric Help You Save Money

At 911 Construction & Electric, we help homeowners in Pasadena and surrounding Los Angeles areas upgrade their electrical panels for EV charger installations. Our licensed electricians will assess your current panel, explain your options, and help you take advantage of available rebates and incentives. We handle everything from permits to final inspection so you can enjoy the benefits of EV charging without the stress.

Contact us today to schedule a panel assessment and learn how much you can save on your EV charger installation in Pasadena and nearby areas. Our team is ready to help you make the right decision for your home and budget.

excerpt.rendered: A panel upgrade can improve safety, support EV charging and all-electric appliances, and may help qualifying homeowners access rebates in Pasadena and nearby Los Angeles areas.

title.rendered: Do You Need a Permit for EV Charger Installation in Los Angeles?

content.rendered:
Do You Need a Permit for EV Charger Installation in Los Angeles?

Most residential EV charger installations in Los Angeles require a permit from the Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety (LADBS). Skipping this step can result in fines, insurance problems, and unsafe work that puts your home and family at risk.

Many homeowners are surprised to learn that permits are not optional for this type of work. Getting the proper permits protects you and ensures the installation meets all safety codes.

What the EV Charger Permit Process Involves

The permit process for EV charger installation in Los Angeles typically includes several steps:

  • Submitting a permit application to LADBS
  • Providing electrical plans and load calculations for review
  • Scheduling and passing a final inspection after installation
  • Ensuring the work meets California Electrical Code requirements
  • Documenting the installation for insurance and future home sales

Working with a licensed, EVITP-certified electrician ensures the entire process goes smoothly and meets all code requirements on the first try.

Why EV Charger Permits Matter in Los Angeles

Getting the proper permit for your EV charger installation is important for several reasons:

  • Avoid fines and stop-work orders from the city
  • Protect your homeowners insurance coverage
  • Ensure the installation is safe and up to code
  • Make future home sales easier with proper documentation
  • Qualify for available rebates and incentives

Skipping the permit process can create serious problems down the road, especially if you ever need to sell your home or file an insurance claim.

We Handle the Entire Permitting Process

911 Construction & Electric manages the complete permitting process for our customers. Our EVITP-certified electricians ensure every installation meets code, qualifies for available incentives, and passes inspection on the first try.

We handle all the paperwork so you can focus on getting your charger installed quickly and safely without the hassle.

Need an EV Charger Installed in Los Angeles?

Contact us today for a permit-ready, code-compliant EV charger installation. We serve homeowners throughout Los Angeles with fast, professional service and full permitting support.

Ready to install your EV charger the right way? Reach out to us and we’ll handle everything from start to finish.

title.rendered: Do You Need a Panel Upgrade for EV Charger Installation in Los Angeles?

content.rendered:
Panel Upgrade for EV Charger Installation in Los Angeles: What You Need to Know

Many homes in Los Angeles need a panel upgrade for EV charger installation. Older 100-amp electrical panels simply cannot handle the power demands of a modern Level 2 EV charger along with your other household appliances.

Without the right upgrade, you risk breaker trips, overheating, and potential safety hazards. A professional electrical panel upgrade ensures your home safely supports fast EV charging.

Why Most LA Homes Need a Panel Upgrade for EV Chargers

Homes built before 2000 often have outdated panels. Adding a Level 2 EV charger (which pulls 30–50 amps) can overload the system. Here are the common warning signs:

  • Frequent breaker trips
  • Flickering or dimming lights
  • Warm or hot electrical panel
  • Inability to add new circuits
  • Old 100-amp panel (especially 30+ years old)

If you see these signs, you will likely need a panel upgrade before installing your EV charger.

Benefits of a Panel Upgrade for EV Charger Installation

  • Safe and reliable Level 2 charging (up to 7x faster than a regular outlet)
  • Support for future electrical needs like smart home devices and appliances
  • Reduced fire risk and better overall electrical safety
  • Higher home resale value in Los Angeles
  • Full compliance with current California Electrical Code

Our Professional EV Charger Panel Upgrade Service

At 911 Construction & Electric (License #1027421), our EVITP certified electricians specialize in panel upgrades for EV charger installation throughout Los Angeles, including Burbank, Pasadena, Glendale, Hollywood, and surrounding areas. 911 Construction & Electric Inc. (EVITP certified electrician)

We handle:

  • Free electrical load assessment and panel evaluation
  • Professional 100 to 200-amp panel upgrades
  • EV charger-ready wiring and installation
  • Smart panel and sub-panel options
  • Full permitting and city inspections
  • Complete LADWP rebate and incentive assistance
  • Same-day and next-day scheduling
  • 24/7 emergency electrical support

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does a panel upgrade for EV charger installation cost in Los Angeles? Costs typically range from $1,500 to $3,500 depending on your home’s needs. We provide a clear quote after a free assessment.

Do I need a permit for a panel upgrade? Yes. We handle all permitting and inspections to ensure full code compliance.

Can I still get LADWP rebates if I upgrade my panel? Yes. We help you maximize rebates when combining a panel upgrade with your EV charger installation.

Ready to safely install your EV charger? Contact us today for a free assessment on your panel upgrade for EV charger installation in Los Angeles.

Call Now: 911 Construction & Electric Inc. (EVITP certified electrician) 747-255-8595

content.rendered:
Electrical Panel Upgrade in Los Angeles: Signs Your Home May Need One

Older electrical panels can create serious safety and performance issues for homeowners throughout Los Angeles and Southern California. As modern homes use more electricity for EV chargers, air conditioning systems, appliances, and smart technology, many older panels struggle to keep up with today’s power demands.

911 Construction & Electric Inc. provides professional electrical panel upgrade services throughout Los Angeles, Pasadena, Glendale, Burbank, and the San Fernando Valley. Our licensed electricians help homeowners improve electrical safety, increase power capacity, and prepare homes for modern electrical needs.

If your home experiences flickering lights, tripped breakers, or overloaded circuits, your electrical panel may no longer safely support your household’s electrical usage.

What Does an Electrical Panel Do?

Your electrical panel distributes electricity throughout your home. It controls power flow to outlets, lighting, appliances, and dedicated circuits.

The panel also protects your home by shutting off power during electrical overloads or short circuits.

As homes add more electrical devices and appliances over time, older panels may become outdated or unsafe.

Signs You May Need an Electrical Panel Upgrade

Many homeowners do not realize their panel is outdated until electrical problems become more noticeable.

Common signs include:

  • Frequent breaker trips
  • Flickering or dimming lights
  • Burning smells near the panel
  • Buzzing sounds from breakers
  • Warm electrical panel surfaces
  • Limited available breaker space
  • Older fuse box systems
  • Appliances causing power fluctuations
  • EV charger installation requirements
  • Home renovations or additions

These issues may indicate overloaded circuits or insufficient electrical capacity.

Why Older Homes Often Need Panel Upgrades

Many homes in Los Angeles, Pasadena, Glendale, and nearby Southern California communities were built decades ago. Older electrical systems were not designed to support modern energy demands.

Today’s homes commonly use:

  • EV chargers
  • Central air conditioning
  • High-powered kitchen appliances
  • Home office equipment
  • Smart home systems
  • Electric water heaters
  • Large entertainment systems

Without adequate electrical capacity, older panels may become overloaded and unsafe.

Is an Outdated Electrical Panel Dangerous?

Yes. Outdated or damaged electrical panels can increase the risk of:

  • Electrical fires
  • Overheating
  • Damaged appliances
  • Power failures
  • Electrical shocks
  • Melted wiring
  • Circuit overloads

Some older electrical panel brands are also known for safety concerns and reliability issues.

Professional inspections help homeowners identify potential hazards before major problems occur.

Benefits of Upgrading Your Electrical Panel

An electrical panel upgrade improves both safety and performance.

Benefits may include:

Improved Electrical Safety

Modern panels provide better protection against overloads and electrical faults.

Increased Power Capacity

Panel upgrades allow homes to safely support modern appliances and EV chargers.

Better Reliability

Upgraded panels reduce breaker trips, power fluctuations, and electrical interruptions.

Support for EV Charger Installation

Many Level 2 EV chargers require additional electrical capacity or dedicated circuits.

Easier Home Renovations

Panel upgrades help support room additions, remodels, and future electrical improvements.

Electrical Panel Upgrades for EV Chargers

As electric vehicle ownership increases across Southern California, many homeowners need panel upgrades before installing Level 2 EV chargers.

EV chargers place significant demand on residential electrical systems. A licensed electrician can determine whether your current panel can safely support EV charging equipment.

911 Construction & Electric Inc. provides:

  • EV charger installation
  • Dedicated EV circuits
  • Panel capacity evaluations
  • Electrical inspections
  • Panel replacements
  • Permit assistance

Common Types of Electrical Panels

Different homes use different electrical systems depending on age and previous upgrades.

Common panel types include:

  • Main breaker panels
  • Subpanels
  • Fuse boxes
  • Split-bus panels
  • Older legacy electrical panels

Some outdated systems may require complete replacement to meet current electrical codes.

Do Electrical Panel Upgrades Require Permits?

Most electrical panel upgrades in Los Angeles require permits and inspections.

Permits help ensure:

  • Code compliance
  • Safe installation practices
  • Proper grounding
  • Correct breaker sizing
  • Utility coordination

Working with a licensed electrician helps homeowners avoid failed inspections and safety risks.

Why Homeowners Choose 911 Construction & Electric Inc.

Homeowners throughout Los Angeles trust 911 Construction & Electric Inc. for professional electrical services and reliable workmanship.

We focus on:

  • Safe installations
  • Code-compliant electrical work
  • Clean job sites
  • Honest recommendations
  • Fast scheduling
  • Long-term electrical safety

Our electricians provide electrical panel upgrades, wiring repairs, EV charger installations, electrical troubleshooting, and safety inspections throughout Southern California.

Areas We Serve

911 Construction & Electric Inc. proudly serves homeowners throughout:

  • Los Angeles
  • Pasadena
  • Glendale
  • Burbank
  • San Fernando Valley
  • Nearby Southern California communities

Schedule an Electrical Panel Inspection

If your home shows signs of electrical problems or you are planning an EV charger installation, a professional electrical inspection can help determine whether your panel needs upgrading.

911 Construction & Electric Inc. provides electrical panel upgrades, EV charger installation, and residential electrical services throughout Los Angeles and surrounding areas.

Contact our team today to schedule an electrical panel inspection or consultation.

FAQ About Electrical Panel Upgrades

How do I know if my electrical panel is outdated?

Frequent breaker trips, flickering lights, buzzing sounds, and limited breaker space may indicate an outdated panel.

Can an old electrical panel cause fires?

Yes. Overloaded or damaged electrical panels can create fire hazards if problems are not corrected.

Do I need a panel upgrade for an EV charger?

Some homes require panel upgrades before installing Level 2 EV chargers depending on available electrical capacity.

How long does an electrical panel upgrade take?

Many residential panel upgrades can be completed within one day, depending on the project scope.

Do electrical panel upgrades increase home value?

Electrical upgrades may improve home safety, reliability, and buyer appeal, especially for older homes.

title.rendered: Top 5 Benefits of Upgrading Your Electrical Panel for EV Charging

content.rendered:
Upgrading your electrical panel is one of the most important steps you can take when installing an EV charger at home. Many older homes in Los Angeles still have 100-amp panels that were never designed to handle the extra load of a Level 2 charger. Without an upgrade, you risk frequent breaker trips, overheating, and even serious safety hazards. A modern panel gives you the capacity and protection you need to charge safely and efficiently.

Beyond safety, a panel upgrade also improves how your home uses electricity. Your EV charger will run at full speed without competing with other appliances, which means faster charging and less strain on your entire electrical system. This upgrade also prepares your home for future technology like home batteries, solar panels, and additional electric vehicles down the road.

Another major benefit is access to rebates and incentives. Many programs in Los Angeles require a properly upgraded panel before you can qualify for thousands of dollars in savings. Skipping the upgrade could mean missing out on money that would have made the installation much more affordable.

Finally, an upgraded panel increases your home’s value and appeal. Buyers are actively looking for homes that are EV-ready. When it comes time to sell, having a modern electrical system with EV charging capability can make your property stand out and sell faster. If you’re planning to install an EV charger, a panel upgrade is one of the smartest investments you can make for both safety and long-term value.

title.rendered: The Complete Guide to Electric Vehicle Charger Installation in Los Angeles

content.rendered:
EV charger installation in Los Angeles has become one of the most requested electrical upgrades for homeowners across Southern California. As more drivers switch to Tesla, Rivian, Ford, BMW, Mercedes-Benz, and other electric vehicles, reliable home charging systems are becoming essential.

911 Construction & Electric Inc. provides professional EV charger installation services throughout Los Angeles, Pasadena, Glendale, Burbank, and the San Fernando Valley. Our licensed electricians help homeowners safely install Level 2 EV chargers, upgrade electrical panels, and prepare homes for long-term EV charging needs.

Whether you recently purchased an electric vehicle or want faster charging at home, understanding the EV charger installation process can help you avoid electrical issues and costly mistakes.

Why EV Charger Installation in Los Angeles Is Growing

Electric vehicle ownership continues to increase throughout Los Angeles and Southern California. Many homeowners prefer charging at home instead of relying on public charging stations.

Home EV charging offers several advantages:

  • Faster charging times

  • Greater convenience

  • Lower charging costs

  • Overnight charging

  • Increased property value

  • Better long-term reliability

Most homeowners choose Level 2 charging systems because they charge vehicles significantly faster than standard wall outlets.

What Is a Level 2 EV Charger?

A Level 2 EV charger uses a dedicated 240-volt electrical circuit to provide faster charging speeds for electric vehicles.

Compared to standard Level 1 charging, Level 2 chargers can dramatically reduce charging time.

Level 2 EV charger installation in Los Angeles often requires:

  • Dedicated 240V circuits

  • Electrical panel evaluations

  • Permit approval

  • Proper breaker sizing

  • Professional wiring installation

A licensed electrician can determine whether your home’s electrical system can safely support EV charging equipment.

EV Charger Installation Los Angeles Requirements

Every home has different electrical requirements. Some installations are simple, while others may require electrical upgrades.

Common EV charger installation requirements include:

Dedicated EV Charging Circuit

Most Level 2 chargers require a dedicated circuit to safely support charging loads.

Electrical Panel Capacity

Older homes may need electrical panel upgrades before installing EV chargers.

Permits and Inspections

Many Los Angeles EV charger installations require permits and inspections to meet electrical code requirements.

Proper Charger Placement

Choosing the right charger location improves convenience while minimizing installation costs.

Older Los Angeles Homes May Need Electrical Upgrades

Many homes across Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, and Burbank were built before EV charging became common. Older electrical systems may not safely support modern charging demands.

During EV charger installation, electricians often identify:

  • Outdated electrical panels

  • Insufficient breaker capacity

  • Loose electrical connections

  • Aging wiring

  • Improper grounding

  • Overloaded circuits

Electrical inspections help identify hidden issues before installation begins.

Electrical Panel Upgrades for EV Chargers

Some homes require panel upgrades before EV charger installation.

An electrical panel upgrade may be necessary if:

  • The panel lacks available breaker space

  • Existing service capacity is too small

  • Older panels cannot safely support additional loads

  • The home uses outdated electrical equipment

Panel upgrades help improve safety while supporting future electrical needs.

Benefits of Professional EV Charger Installation

Professional EV charger installation in Los Angeles helps homeowners avoid safety issues and failed inspections.

Licensed electricians help ensure:

  • Proper wire sizing

  • Safe breaker installation

  • Correct grounding

  • Code compliance

  • Reliable charging performance

  • Permit approval

Improper EV charger installation can create electrical hazards or damage expensive charging equipment.

EV Charger Rebates and Incentives

Some homeowners may qualify for EV charger rebates or tax incentives depending on utility programs and current regulations.

The Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP) provides information regarding EV charger rebates and incentive programs for qualifying customers. (ladwp.com)

Homeowners should verify current eligibility requirements before installation.

EV Charger Installation for Tesla and Other EV Brands

911 Construction & Electric Inc. installs charging equipment for many electric vehicle brands, including:

  • Tesla

  • Rivian

  • Ford

  • Chevrolet

  • BMW

  • Mercedes-Benz

  • Hyundai

  • Kia

  • Lucid

Different vehicles and chargers may require different electrical configurations depending on charging speed and equipment specifications.

Why Homeowners Choose 911 Construction & Electric Inc.

Homeowners throughout Los Angeles trust 911 Construction & Electric Inc. for professional electrical services and safe EV charger installations.

We focus on:

  • Code-compliant electrical work

  • Safe installations

  • Clean workmanship

  • Honest recommendations

  • Fast scheduling

  • Long-term electrical safety

Our electricians provide EV charger installation, electrical panel upgrades, surge protection, wiring repairs, and residential electrical services throughout Southern California.

Areas We Serve

911 Construction & Electric Inc. proudly serves homeowners throughout:

  • Los Angeles

  • Pasadena

  • Glendale

  • Burbank

  • San Fernando Valley

  • Nearby Southern California communities

Schedule EV Charger Installation in Los Angeles

If you are planning to install a home EV charger, working with an experienced electrician helps ensure a safe and reliable installation process.

911 Construction & Electric Inc. provides EV charger installation, panel upgrades, electrical inspections, and residential electrical services throughout Los Angeles and surrounding Southern California areas.

Contact our team today to schedule an EV charger installation consultation.

FAQ About EV Charger Installation Los Angeles

How much does EV charger installation cost in Los Angeles?

Installation costs vary depending on panel capacity, wiring distance, permit requirements, and charger type.

Do I need a permit for EV charger installation in Los Angeles?

Many EV charger installations require permits and inspections for code compliance.

Can older homes support EV chargers?

Many older homes can support EV chargers, but some require panel upgrades or electrical improvements.

How long does EV charger installation take?

Some installations can be completed in a few hours, while more complex projects may require additional electrical upgrades.

Should I install a Level 2 EV charger?

Most homeowners prefer Level 2 chargers because they provide significantly faster charging compared to standard outlets.

title.rendered: Do Los Angeles Homes Need GFCI Outlet Upgrades?

content.rendered:
Why Los Angeles Homes Need GFCI Outlet Upgrades

Living in Los Angeles means dealing with older homes in many neighborhoods — from Burbank to Hollywood, Glendale, Pasadena, and beyond. If your house was built before the 1990s, chances are your electrical outlets in wet areas still use standard receptacles instead of modern GFCI (Ground Fault Circuit Interrupter) protection.

GFCI outlets are life-saving devices that instantly cut power if they detect a ground fault — such as when electricity comes in contact with water — preventing severe shocks and reducing the risk of electrical fires.

Where Are GFCI Outlets Required in California?

According to the California Electrical Code, GFCI protection is mandatory in:

  • Bathrooms (all outlets, especially near sinks)
  • Kitchens (countertops and within 6 feet of sinks)
  • Garages and basements
  • Laundry rooms and utility areas
  • Outdoor outlets (patios, gardens, pool areas)
  • Wet bars or any location near water

Many older LA homes are not up to current standards. Upgrading isn’t just smart — it’s often required during home sales, insurance reviews, or renovations.

Benefits of Upgrading to GFCI Outlets

  • Enhanced Family Safety — Critical protection for children, elderly family members, and daily use
  • Code Compliance — Avoid failed inspections and potential fines
  • Fire Prevention — Significantly lowers electrical fire risks
  • Increased Home Value — Makes your property more attractive to buyers
  • Peace of Mind — Especially important in earthquake-prone Southern California

GFCI upgrades are one of the most affordable and impactful electrical improvements you can make.

Professional GFCI Outlet Installation in Los Angeles

At 911 Construction & Electric, our licensed electricians (License #1027421) specialize in safe, code-compliant GFCI upgrades across the Los Angeles area. We:

  • Perform a thorough inspection of your existing outlets
  • Install high-quality tamper-resistant GFCI receptacles
  • Properly wire and protect downstream outlets
  • Offer same-day or next-day service on most jobs
  • Provide 24/7 emergency electrical support

Whether you need just a few outlets upgraded or a full-home safety audit, we’ve got you covered.

Ready to upgrade your outlets? Contact us today for a free quote on GFCI outlet installation in Los Angeles.

Call Now: 747-255-8595

title.rendered: Pasadena EV Charger Rebate: What Homeowners Should Know

content.rendered:
Pasadena EV Charger Rebate: What Homeowners Should Know in 2026

Pasadena homeowners can significantly reduce the cost of going electric with generous rebates from Pasadena Water and Power (PWP). Installing a home EV charger not only makes charging your electric vehicle convenient and affordable — it also qualifies you for valuable local incentives.

Current Pasadena EV Charger Rebates (2026)

  • $600 Rebate — For a qualifying Wi-Fi enabled or Internet-connected Level 2 EV charger
  • $200 Rebate — For a standard (non-Wi-Fi) Level 2 charger

These rebates are available to PWP residential electric customers. Additional incentives may be available for income-qualified households. Note: The federal residential EV charger tax credit (30% up to $1,000) is scheduled to end for projects after June 30, 2026 — so now is a great time to act.

Why Install a Level 2 EV Charger in Pasadena?

  • Charge your EV up to 7x faster than a standard outlet
  • Convenient overnight charging at home
  • Lower long-term fuel and maintenance costs
  • Increase your home’s resale value
  • Support cleaner air in the Pasadena area

Most modern EVs (Tesla, Ford, GM, Hyundai, etc.) work great with Level 2 chargers.

Benefits of Working with 911 Construction & Electric

At 911 Construction & Electric (License #1027421), we specialize in professional EV charger installations throughout Pasadena and surrounding areas. Our licensed electricians provide:

  • Free site evaluation and load assessment
  • Panel upgrade recommendations if needed
  • High-quality Level 2 charger installation (hardwired or plug-in)
  • Full permit acquisition and code compliance
  • Complete rebate paperwork assistance
  • Same-day and next-day scheduling options
  • 24/7 emergency electrical support

We handle everything from start to finish so you can focus on enjoying your new EV charger and claiming your rebate.

Ready to save money and go electric? Contact us today for a free quote on EV charger installation and rebate assistance in Pasadena.

Call Now: 747-255-8595

title.rendered: Why Los Angeles Homeowners Are Installing EV Chargers at Home

content.rendered:
Why Install a Home EV Charger in Los Angeles?

With more Angelenos switching to electric vehicles every day, having a reliable home charging station is no longer a luxury — it’s a necessity. A Level 2 EV charger lets you charge your vehicle up to 7 times faster than a standard outlet, typically adding 25-60 miles of range per hour.

At 911 Construction & Electric, we provide professional, code-compliant home EV charger installations across Los Angeles, including Burbank, Hollywood, Glendale, Pasadena, and surrounding areas.

LADWP EV Charger Rebates & Incentives (2026)

Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP) customers can save significantly:

  • Up to $1,000 rebate on qualifying Level 2 EV chargers
  • Up to $1,500 total for customers in Lifeline or EZ-SAVE programs
  • $250 additional rebate for installing a dedicated EV meter
  • Federal Tax Credit (30C) up to $1,000 for chargers installed by June 30, 2026

We help you maximize these savings by handling the entire process — from charger selection to rebate paperwork.

Benefits of a Professional Level 2 EV Charger Installation

  • Faster charging (full charge in 4-8 hours vs. 24+ on a regular outlet)
  • Increased home value and buyer appeal
  • Lower long-term energy costs with Time-of-Use rates
  • Safe, reliable, and future-proof installation
  • Support for all major EV brands (Tesla, Ford, GM, Hyundai, Rivian, etc.)

Our Home EV Charger Installation Services in Los Angeles

Our licensed electricians (License #1027421) handle every step:

  • Free home evaluation and electrical load assessment
  • Panel upgrade recommendations (if needed)
  • Hardwired or plug-in Level 2 charger installation
  • Smart Wi-Fi enabled chargers for app control and scheduling
  • Full city permitting and inspections
  • Complete rebate and tax credit assistance
  • Same-day and next-day scheduling available
  • 24/7 emergency electrical support

Whether you have a single-family home, townhouse, or condo, we deliver safe and efficient installations tailored to your needs.

Ready to charge smarter at home? Contact us today for a free quote on professional EV charger installation in Los Angeles.

Call Now: 747-255-8595

title.rendered: Why Hiring an EVITP Certified Installer Matters in Los Angeles

content.rendered:
Why EVITP Certification Matters for EV Charger Installation in Los Angeles

When installing a home or business EV charger in Los Angeles, not all electricians are equal. EVITP certification (Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Training Program) is the gold standard for professionals who install Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE).

EVITP is a specialized training and certification program that goes far beyond standard electrical licensing. It equips electricians with in-depth knowledge of EV charger installation best practices, safety protocols, National Electrical Code (NEC) requirements specific to EVs, and proper load management.

Key Reasons to Choose an EVITP Certified Installer

  • Rebate & Incentive Eligibility Many Los Angeles programs (LADWP, Pasadena Water & Power, and California statewide incentives) require EVITP certification to qualify for rebates up to $1,500 or more. Non-certified installations may be denied.
  • Safety & Code Compliance EV chargers involve high-voltage circuits, proper grounding, GFCI protection, and sophisticated communication with vehicles. EVITP-certified electricians are trained to prevent hazards like overheating, fire risks, or electrical faults.
  • Faster Approvals & Inspections Certified installers understand local permitting requirements, helping your project pass inspection the first time and avoid delays.
  • Future-Proof Installation Proper training ensures your charger supports today’s and tomorrow’s EVs, including smart features, Wi-Fi connectivity, and higher power levels.
  • Protection for Your Home & Investment Avoid costly mistakes that could damage your electrical panel, void warranties, or create safety issues down the road.

What EVITP Certification Involves

EVITP is a rigorous 20+ hour program plus exam for licensed electricians. Topics include:

  • EV charging fundamentals
  • NEC Article 625 requirements
  • Site assessment and load calculations
  • Safety and grounding standards
  • Troubleshooting and maintenance

At 911 Construction & Electric (License #1027421), our electricians are EVITP certified, ensuring every installation meets the highest industry standards.

Professional EV Charger Installation You Can Trust

We provide full-service EV charger solutions across Los Angeles, Burbank, Pasadena, Glendale, Hollywood, and surrounding areas:

  • Free site evaluation and electrical assessment
  • Panel upgrades when needed
  • Smart Level 2 charger installation (hardwired or plug-in)
  • Permit handling and rebate paperwork assistance
  • Same-day and next-day availability
  • 24/7 emergency electrical support

Don’t risk your rebate or safety with a non-certified installer. Hire professionals who are specifically trained for EV charger work.

Ready for a safe, certified installation? Contact us today for a free quote.

Call Now: 747-255-8595

title.rendered: Signs You Need an Electrical Panel Upgrade in Los Angeles

content.rendered:
Signs You Need an Electrical Panel Upgrade in Los Angeles

Many older homes in Los Angeles — from Burbank and Glendale to Hollywood and Pasadena — still use outdated electrical panels. These panels often cannot handle modern power demands from EVs, home offices, smart appliances, and air conditioning.

Watch for these 7 warning signs. They show it’s time to upgrade your electrical panel.

7 Warning Signs Your Electrical Panel Needs Upgrading

  1. Frequent Breaker Trips Breakers that trip often when you run multiple appliances or an EV charger mean your panel is overloaded.
  2. Flickering or Dimming Lights Lights that flicker or dim when you turn on high-power devices signal voltage problems from an old panel.
  3. Warm or Hot Electrical Panel A warm panel is dangerous. It warns of overloaded circuits and raises fire risk.
  4. Outdated or Old Panel If your panel is 30+ years old — especially Federal Pacific, Zinsco, or Pushmatic brands — replace it immediately.
  5. Burning Smell or Discoloration A burning smell, buzzing sounds, or scorch marks near the panel require urgent professional help.
  6. Cannot Add New Circuits If an electrician cannot add a new EV charger, sub-panel, or AC unit, your main panel lacks enough capacity.
  7. Heavy Use of Extension Cords Relying on extension cords and power strips throughout your home often means your panel is overloaded.

Why Upgrade Your Electrical Panel Now?

  • You improve home safety and reduce fire risk
  • You support modern appliances and EV chargers
  • You increase your home’s resale value
  • You meet current California Electrical Code requirements

Professional Electrical Panel Upgrades in Los Angeles

At 911 Construction & Electric (California License #1027421), our licensed electricians specialize in safe panel upgrades across Los Angeles.

We offer:

  • Free electrical panel assessment
  • 100–200 amp panel upgrades
  • Smart panel and sub-panel installations
  • EV charger-ready upgrades
  • Full permitting and inspection handling
  • Same-day and next-day service
  • 24/7 emergency support

Don’t wait for a serious problem. Schedule your free panel assessment today.

Call Now: 747-255-8595
